newsitem.title: CHINA: Many Chinese farmers don't farm, says academy.
newsitem.headline: Many Chinese farmers don't farm, says academy.

text.p: Many of China's farmers no longer make their living from the land and should be called something else, the official Xinhua news agency on Monday quoted the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences as saying.

While it had long been generally accepted that China had 900 million farmers, the term "farmer" should in fact refer only to those engaged in agriculture -- not just anyone living in the countryside, Xinhua quoted researcher Yao Mei as saying.
An academy study had found that China's rural labour force was 460 million strong, of whom just 250 million people were engaged in agricultural production, the agency said.
More than 100 million rural residents were working in township firms and a further 80 million were migrants labouring in urban areas, it said but gave no details of the remainder.

The academy's study had pointed out the necessity of distinguishing between farmers, the agricultural population and the rural population -- all of which had been lumped together for decades, Xinhua said.
Under China's rigid pre-reform state-planned economy, farmers were not allowed to look for work on their own but were tied to the soil, it quoted Yao as saying.

From the day they were born, they were naturally regarded as farmers, she said, adding that under a decade and a half of economic reforms that have opened up wide sectors of the economy many farmers have begun taking jobs outside the agricultural sector.
